items.summary: Nuclear reactors may go dark, but their fuel continues producing a faint antineutrino “glow” long after shutdown. items.summary: Scientists have discovered that the aging human brain may be far less isolated from the rest of the body than once believed. items.title: Neptune’s tiny moons may be the wreckage of shattered ancient worlds
items.summary: JWST has uncovered surprising clues that Neptune’s strange inner moons may be the wreckage of an ancient cosmic catastrophe. Researchers detected clay-like minerals on Larissa, Galatea, and Neptune’s rings that form in the presence of liquid water—yet the moons themselves show no obvious water ice.

items.title: Common food preservative linked to rising suicide deaths among young people
items.summary: A widely available food-preservation chemical is emerging as a disturbing factor in rising UK suicide deaths, particularly among younger people and men. Researchers say the scale may be underestimated and are calling for urgent restrictions on access and harmful online information.
